title: K-flatness of an exhaustive complex built from split free cells
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring, and let $C$ be an integer cochain complex of $R$-modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Suppose there is an increasing sequence of subcomplexes
$$0=C_0\subseteq C_1\subseteq C_2\subseteq\cdots\subseteq C$$
such that every element of every $C^n$ belongs to some $C_m^n$. Assume each inclusion $C_m^n\hookrightarrow C_{m+1}^n$ has an $R$-linear retraction, and the quotient complex $C_{m+1}/C_m$ has zero differential and free modules in every degree [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. Then $C$ is K-flat [def-pc-module-kflat-complex]: for every acyclic cochain complex $A$ of $R$-modules, the signed direct-sum total tensor complex $\operatorname{Tot}(A\otimes_R C)$ is acyclic. No bound on the cochain degrees or the ranks of the free modules is assumed.

source.place: Tags 0BYH (lemma-K-flat-two-out-of-three-ses) and 06Y3 (lemma-colimit-K-flat), with the zero-differential free-quotient argument in the proof of lemma-resolution-filtered-complex; read cached more-algebra.tex lines 14255–14338 and 15755–15764 in /home/ubuntu/c1-stacks-review/.

proof.text: Apply the finite-stage induction theorem to the sequence F, step. It gives K-flatness of every F m from hzero, the degreewise retractions, and the zero-differential free quotient hypotheses.

Apply the exhaustive-colimit theorem to the inclusions ι and transition maps step. The monicity, compatibility and exhaustion identify C with the filtered union, and the theorem transports K-flatness from all finite stages to C.
